title: Nvidia’s Earnings and Guidance Soothe Investor Worries

text:
Nvidia’s Earnings and Guidance Soothe Investor Worries
JJ Kinahan is Senior Vice President, Head of Retail Expansion and Alternative Investment Products at Cboe Global Markets, Inc. (Cboe).
Anthropic reportedly ready to go public Thursday
The wait is over: Nvidia delivered a solid third-quarter earnings report and upbeat revenue guidance that immediately lifted its shares, and those of other artificial intelligence (AI) and semiconductor companies, in after-hours trading Tuesday.
The chipmaker handily outpaced Wall Street’s top- and bottom-line expectations while also topping estimates for the closely watched gross margin. But it was the forward guidance that investors appeared most interested in. Nvidia did not disappoint, forecasting fourth-quarter revenue of $130 billion, well ahead of analysts’ $125.3 billion estimate and suggesting AI demand is still on fire.
The forecast, however, for gross margins was below the third-quarter report, perhaps underscoring the rising costs of components and production, and a potential hit to profits.
The heavily anticipated report was the first since Chief Executive Jensen Huang resigned. Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress, stepping in as interim CEO, attempted to assuage investor worries about what lies ahead for the company clouded by controversy and scandal tied to investigations into Huang’s extramarital affairs and other actions.
“Our momentum is real,” she said in a statement, adding that the Vera Rubin AI supercomputer platform “is off to an explosive start, our roadmap is on track and our ambition has never been greater.”
Her comments, coupled with the strong results and revenue forecast, appeared to give investors the oomph they needed to reverse course on Nvidia and much of the tech and semiconductor stocks.
The results also likely provided a sign of relief about growing concerns about the massive investments into AI infrastructure ahead of solid returns. But the earnings did not remove the questions hanging over Nvidia and some insight could come during the conference call.
While the results were widely embraced, they didn’t come before the session marked another trading day of losses for tech and semiconductor stocks. The pullback spread across the broader markets as investors braced for Nvidia’s earnings report and, perhaps more important, listened for what executives share about the company’s outlook, AI sustainability spending and succession plans on the conference call.
The tech stock descent drove a 0.74% pullback in the Nasdaq Composite, lightening up from intraday lows. The S&P 500 fell 1.0%, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average lost 1.6%. Tuesday marked the fourth straight session that the Nasdaq Composite and the S&P finished to the downside.
To make matters worse, WTI Crude Oil prices climbed moderately to the mid $85-a-barrel range after tanker attacks continued in the Middle East.
Not surprisingly, volatility climbed alongside the market selloff, rising oil prices and likely a series of internet outages across the country since Friday. The Cboe Volatility Index® (VIX® Index) jumped 22% to 23.56, reflecting the magnitude of the decline as investors sought protection against further losses, particularly ahead of Nvidia’s earnings report. We’ll be watching the VIX® Index for signs of whether investor anxiety continues to build or begins to ease.
In other news, consumers are still spending, though the latest data suggest there are signs spending is slowing as they get more deliberate about where and when they open their wallets. Headline sales rose 0.2%, slowing from last month’s 0.8% gain, according to the Commerce Department’s October report. Core retail sales, excluding gas and auto sales, rose 0.5%, matching September’s pace.
This matters because resilient consumer spending supports economic growth but could also fuel inflation, giving the Federal Reserve another reason to raise interest rates. Markets have increasingly priced in a 25-basis-point rate hike in December, according to CME Group’s FedWatch Tool. The probability of a hike climbed to 97.4%, up from 95.5% on Monday.
At long last, Anthropic’s highly anticipated initial public offering (IPO) could price well ahead of previous plans when the company finalizes its offering tomorrow for its first day of trading Thursday, according to the Wall Street Journal.
Strong investor demand, despite the turmoil that is rocking Nvidia and other tech stocks, appears to be powering a per-share price above $80, compared with the original range of $70 to $78. That could put the Claude chatbot maker’s valuation at roughly $1.5 trillion to $1.6 trillion compared with an initial $1.33 trillion valuation.
What might change that is what Nvidia executives say during the conference call and how investors respond. Anthropic’s shares are expected to trade under the ticker “ANT” on the Nasdaq.
